summary: 802.1X authentication failing on CORPORATE-SSID after RADIUS certificate rotation; VPN connections not re-establishing
description: Issue summary: At ~08:20 PST on 2026-03-10 a subset of employees across the SF office reported inability to join CORPORATE-SSID (WPA2-Enterprise / 802.1X). Affected clients fell back to GUEST-SSID or had no network. Concurrently, several users reported their VPN (CompanyVPN / OpenConnect) failed to re-establish after being kicked off by the Wi-Fi drop. Impact: ~120 users intermittently affected (most on macOS 13/14 and some Android 13 devices). Core services (git, Slack, internal apps) were inaccessible for those users. Environment: production corporate Wi-Fi using Mist APs, RADIUS cluster (FreeRADIUS) behind HA proxy, Okta as identity provider for EAP-PEAP/MSCHAPv2, OpenConnect VPN appliances for remote access. Timeline: 08:00 — automated cert rotation for RADIUS completed; 08:18 — first auth failures; 08:22 — ticket opened; 08:45 — temporary mitigation applied; ongoing. Observed behaviour: RADIUS rejects EAP exchanges with TLS handshake failures referencing certificate trust or SAN mismatch. VPN clients do not prompt for re-auth and remain in CONNECTING state or immediately drop. Expected behaviour: seamless re-auth to WLAN and VPN after cert rotation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure device is configured for CORPORATE-SSID (WPA2-Enterprise, PEAP/MSCHAPv2).
2) Trigger re-auth by toggling Wi-Fi or forcing association to corporate SSID.
3) Observe client attempts EAP exchange and either times out or receives TLS handshake failure from RADIUS.
4) If VPN client was active, note it attempts to reconnect and either stalls or fails without credential prompt.
logs: Mar 10 08:19:02 radius1 freeradius[2245]: EAP-PEAP: TLS alert received: fatal (42) - certificate_unknown
Mar 10 08:19:02 radius1 freeradius[2245]: rlm_eap: TLS handshake error: certificate verify failed (unknown_ca)
Mar 10 08:20:10 haproxy[1312]: CONNECT to radius-backend/10.10.2.23:1812 failed: TLS handshake error
Client (macbook-pro): wpa_supplicant: EAP: TLS - received fatal alert: certificate_unknown
VPN appliance: openconnect[pid]: TLS handshake failed: server cert validation error
investigation_notes: 08:25 - Confirmed rotation job ran at 08:00; new RADIUS leaf cert issued by internal CA with expiry 2027-03-09.
08:30 - Observed mismatch between RADIUS server cert SANs and the hostnames used by HAProxy health checks; some APs are configured to validate a different FQDN.
08:35 - NTP skew detected (~6 minutes) on radius2 (10.10.2.24) causing client TLS validation failures on devices strict about time sync.
08:40 - Okta SSO console shows no policy changes; certificate chain presented to clients missing intermediate CA on one RADIUS node (radius2).
08:42 - Cross-checked cert bundles: radius1 and radius3 have full chain; radius2 certificate bundle was missing intermediate due to packaging script bug in rotation job.

Hypothesis: Incomplete cert chain on radius2 + NTP skew caused a subset of APs (that prefer radius2 via session stickiness) to return validate-failed responses, leading clients to drop and VPN clients to fail reconnect without prompting.
mitigation: 08:45 - Temporarily rolled back HAProxy pool to exclude radius2; auth success rate on APs increased to normal within 90s.
09:05 - Reissued complete cert bundle for radius2 with intermediate included and corrected NTP (systemd-timesyncd restarted and compared to ntp.redwood.net).
09:15 - Reintroduced radius2 to HAProxy with weight reduced; monitored for 30 minutes — no TLS errors observed in logs post-fix.

Workaround for users: Connect to wired network where available or manually select GUEST-SSID then reconnect to CORPORATE-SSID after 2-3 minutes; VPN users can kill and restart OpenConnect to force credential prompt if needed.
resolution: Partial resolution applied 2026-03-10: radius2 cert bundle reissued with correct intermediate chain and NTP resynchronized. HAProxy restore completed at 09:15 PST and auth success rate returned to baseline. Follow-up remediation planned: audit and harden cert rotation job to validate bundle completeness, add pre-flight checks for NTP across radius nodes, and add health-check to HAProxy to fail a backend when cert chain validation fails. Owners: Infra Sec (cert rotation) and Network SRE. Postmortem scheduled and linked (see related_confluence_pages).
